title: Compensate conveyor-oven transport delay with a Smith predictor
physicalPurpose: Control downstream product temperature without repeatedly correcting for heater action still travelling through the oven.
principalTechnique: Qualified ordinary PI followed by Smith prediction and model-mismatch validation
objective: Qualify the strongest acceptable ordinary proportional-integral controller, design a Smith predictor from an independently validated delayed plant model, and decide whether its nominal benefit remains acceptable when process gain, time constant, or transport delay differs from that model.

simplifications: One local first-order-plus-dead-time product-temperature path around fixed belt speed and airflow
The declared inlet-temperature event directly changes the local thermal state
One ideal bounded heater request with actuator lag and slew but no installed-valve nonlinearity
Internal model parameters remain nominal while test-only plant cases declare mismatch
Simulation-only I/O and evidence; no physical oven is operated

baseline.limitation: The highest-bandwidth ordinary PI that passes the robustness envelope still reacts only after the downstream sensor sees transported heater action.

change.decision: Accept prediction only when its nominal improvement, mismatch degradation, correction limit and deterministic measured-feedback fallback are all visible.

disturbances: Apply a -2 degC inlet-temperature disturbance at 70 s
Repeat with moderate actual gain 0.76 degC/%, time constant 13 s and delay 17 s
Repeat with severe actual gain 0.60 degC/%, time constant 18 s and delay 22 s

acceptance.window: time from the 10-s request until first reaching 33.5 degC
mean absolute error from 170 through 180 s after settling qualification
10 through 180 s in the severe-mismatch run

abortPredicates: Any required signal is nonfinite, stale, forced, or invalid
Measured or predicted temperature leaves 15 through 60 degC
Predictor remains active with incomplete history or invalid model state
safety.restorationMode: Disable prediction, return to measured feedback, ramp simulated heater request to zero, restore 20 degC, then requalify data and model before a new run.
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised oven controls engineer and responsible process owner
simulationOnlyRestrictions: No physical oven, belt or heater is operated
Simulation model truth is not identified-model or physical-plant evidence
Physical testing requires reviewed heater capacity, product limits, airflow, belt speed, fire protection, topology, abort/restoration plan and explicit approval

video.viewerOutcome: Qualify ordinary feedback, design Smith prediction, and reject unsafe confidence when model mismatch consumes the declared validity envelope.

learning.context: A continuous food-drying conveyor has a downstream product-temperature sensor sixteen seconds of transport after its heater.
learning.reason: Unlike Lesson 58's operating-point dependence, this locally consistent plant is limited by unobserved heater action in transit.
theory: The delayed FOPDT balance uses an earlier heater command.
The strongest ordinary PI is selected from robustness evidence, not nominal IAE alone.
A Smith predictor combines a delay-free model with measured-minus-delayed-model correction and falls back when that evidence is invalid.
learning.workedPrediction: A 10-percent heater step eventually raises temperature 8 degC, produces no downstream response for 16 s, and reaches about 63 percent of that rise over the following 12 s.
practicalPreparation: Verify Simulation evidence, identities, units, quality, timing, heater limits, model envelope, history, correction and fallback.
Define IAE, overshoot, settling, final error, heater travel, active fraction, correction and fallback before results.
learning.baseline: Reject the next-more-aggressive ordinary PI and retain the highest-bandwidth candidate satisfying nominal and perturbed requirements.
learning.change: Use the validated delay-free and delayed models to provide Smith-predicted feedback with bounded correction and measured-feedback fallback.
learning.comparison: Hold operating state, demand, disturbance, limits, timing, seed and windows equal; declare tuning and plant-model changes explicitly.
learning.validation: Require nominal Smith control to reach 90 percent of the requested temperature rise at least 15 percent sooner and to have lower setpoint-window integral absolute error than accepted ordinary feedback, bounded moderate mismatch degradation, and deterministic fallback under severe mismatch.
learning.explanation: Prediction accounts for heater action still in transit; correction anchors the model, while mismatch exposes why physical delay was never removed.
learning.transfer: Use Smith prediction only with a validated uncertainty envelope; Lesson 60 diagnoses a nonlinear or sticking final element.
